messages:
maria_support: Customer CH-842 reported they found what looks like a Redwood API token pasted in a public Pastebin entry. customer pasted the snippet in the ticket, says it was an internal dev who accidentally posted. they want immediate guidance and the key revoked. partial token shown: sk-live-***a7f3

jon_sre: thanks. can you confirm whether that key is for their hosted account or a dedicated/private deploy? need account id and the key id. also ask if they saw any unusual usage spikes.

maria_support: confirmed: hosted account, account id 7721. customer checked dashboard and sees a few thousand requests in a 3-hour window overnight they didn't trigger. they attached an example request id: req_0a9f3b2c.

vishal_sec: mark as high. immediate actions: 1) rotate the compromised key (create new key + revoke old) 2) generate an audit package for compliance (logs + IPs + request ids) 3) check KMS/HSM wrap status for existing keys and whether there were any key operations. ping rotations-bot to run the standard emergency rotate flow. also enable temporary rate limits if abuse ongoing.

eng_oncall: +1 to rate-limit. i'll add a temporary rule to throttle keys from suspicious IP ranges. which region were the requests from?

maria_support: customer says majority from us-east-1 ip ranges. they already disabled the key on their side but want us to fully revoke on our side and provide an audit export for their SOC.

rotations-bot: auto-response: received rotate request for account 7721. to rotate API key run: ```curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/internal/keys/rotate -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" -d '{"account_id":7721, "reason":"reported public pastebin leak"}'``` Expected output: {"new_key_id":"k_9f3...","status":"scheduled"}. Will not auto-revoke until a human confirms.

jon_sre: do NOT run the rotate without confirming with sec and support. rotation-bot, stage the rotation and mark pending. vishal, can you confirm whether we need a KMS HSM key rotation too? if so, ops needs a heads-up.

vishal_sec: KMS/HSM: the customer is hosted (we manage the key material) but the leak is an API credential, not the HSM key material. we do NOT need to rotate HSM keys. we DO need to: - revoke the compromised API key server-side - create a new key with limited scope and short expiry for the customer to test - produce audit logs (last 30 days) for account 7721 and export S3 bundle for SOC. also prepare an incident memo for compliance (data retention and whether any customer data was accessed).

maria_support: customer asks for exact timeline: when we revoke, how long until old key can no longer make requests? and they want a signed statement for auditors.

eng_oncall: revoke is immediate on our side (token blacklist effective within seconds), however caches at edge may allow a few in-flight requests (usually <1 min). i'll coordinate the throttle rule too.

vishal_sec: i'll draft the signed statement. include: time of report, time of revocation, steps taken (rotation, audit export, HSM check), and indicator if any data egress occurred. give me 2 hours.

jon_sre: for repro / troubleshooting: request ids we have: req_0a9f3b2c, req_1b8d2e4f. check traces in the observability console -> traces -> account 7721 -> filter by request id. look for HEADERS X-Forwarded-For and token usage. also check billing spikes: if token abused for embeddings it can cause high costs — flag billing for review.

maria_support: passing steps to customer so they can rotate on their side too. will follow up when they confirm.

vishal_sec: follow-ups: 1) rotate server-side now once customer confirms they have rotated locally 2) generate audit export and put S3 link into secure ticket 3) redact any leaked snippets from customer attachments stored in our ticketing system 4) ask customer to rotate any downstream services that used the token 5) create short post-incident note for compliance.

eng_oncall: done: temporary throttle applied to account 7721 and us-east-1 CIDR ranges we saw. revocation to be executed after confirmation.

maria_support: customer confirmed they've removed the paste and rotated keys on their side. requesting us to proceed.

vishal_sec: proceeding with revoke. rotations-bot please run: POST /internal/keys/revoke {"account_id":7721, "key_mask":"sk-live-***a7f3"} and then generate audit export for 7721.

rotations-bot: action: revoke scheduled -> running... action: revoke completed at 1781234625. new key created k_9f3_test (sent to customer via secure channel). audit export: s3://redwood-exports/7721/incident-1781234567-export.tar.gz (access: internal-only).

maria_support: confirmed with customer that new key received and tests passed. customer requests the signed statement PDF.

vishal_sec: I uploaded the incident memo to the secure ticket and emailed signed copy to the customer's security contact. I noted retention policy: logs exported are within 90-day retention window; if auditors need older data we will do legal/retention escalation.

jon_sre: closing tasks: - remove temporary throttle after 24h if no further anomalies - mark old key as revoked in billing to prevent any retro charges - attach trace snippets to ticket.

maria_support: thanks team :thumbsup: closing this thread once customer acknowledges receipt of signed memo.
